title: Chapter 16 — The Brand Ladder and Tiering
intro: Tiers, brand identities, family trees, and how to answer the brand question honestly.

sections.title: Understanding the Tiers
sections.content:
The appliance market has distinct tiers: value, mid-range, premium, and luxury. Each tier serves a different customer with different priorities.

Value: function and price matter most. Mid-range: balance of features and reliability. Premium: performance, design, and brand. Luxury: no-compromise materials, craftsmanship, and prestige.

Knowing which brands sit in which tier — and why — helps you match the customer to the right product without overselling or underselling.

sections.title: Answering the Brand Question
sections.content:
Customers often ask: 'What brand is the best?' That question has no honest single answer. The best brand depends on the customer's priorities, budget, and category.

The honest response: 'It depends on what matters most to you. Let me ask a few questions so I can point you in the right direction.'

That brings you back to discovery — where every good recommendation starts.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating brand knowledge, ask:

Can the salesperson explain the tier structure clearly?
Do they match brands to customer priorities — not personal preference?
Do they answer brand questions honestly — admitting that 'best' depends on the buyer?
Do they understand brand family trees and which parent companies own which brands?
